## Summary
- `import_settings()` passes setting data directly to the `Setting` constructor, but the `type` field arrives as a string (e.g. `"APP"`) from JSON defaults and exports, while the DB column expects a `SettingType` enum. This could cause `AttributeError` on `.name` access in `get_all_settings()`.
- Fixes the root cause by converting the string to enum **at the point of import** in both `web/services/settings_manager.py` and `settings/manager.py`
- Removes the `hasattr` fallback guard added in #2073, since the type will now always be a proper enum when read back from the database

- [x] 981 settings/web tests pass
- [x] Pre-commit hooks pass

author: sudrao88
body:
Fix Local AI Index broken after OTA by downloading ALL build output f…iles

The OTA download previously discovered assets by parsing HTML, Vite manifest, and CSS url() references. This missed files only referenced at runtime — worker chunks (embedding.worker), WASM binaries (onnxruntime-web), and dynamic imports. After OTA, these files were absent, causing the Web Worker to fail with "Unknown Worker Error".

Fix: generate ota-manifest.json at build time (in generate-version.js) that lists every file in dist/. OTADownloadManager now uses this as the primary download source, with the old HTML/Vite parsing as fallback for older deploys.

body: In #392, I added the `chestxray14_binary_classification.ipynb` and `chestxray14_multilabel_classification.ipynb` examples. This PR cleans up three issues with these example notebooks. 1. PyHealth Install 2. GitHub Display 3. Duplicate Output ## 1. PyHealth Install Previously, these notebooks installed PyHealth from a branch in my fork. Now that #392 is merged AND 2.0.0 is released, that can be cleaned up. **Before** ```py !rm -rf PyHealth !git clone https://github.com/EricSchrock/PyHealth.git %cd PyHealth !git checkout ChestX-ray14 !pip install -e . ``` **After** ```py %pip install pyhealth ipywidgets ``` > [!CAUTION] > Is it a surprise that `ipywidgets` must also be explicitly installed? I get an error in `base_dataset.py` if I just `pip install pyhealth`. ## 2. GitHub Display I initially generated these notebooks in Google Colab. Apparently, this added a bunch of metadata, which wasn't compatible with the GitHub web UI. Trying to view the notebooks on GitHub would show the following. This PR should fix the issue. ## 3. Duplicate Output The old versions of the example notebooks printed every output twice, which makes the example much longer and less clear. Apparently, I didn't have Google Colab properly configured to work with the Python logger. This PR fixes the duplicate output.

body:
New Files Created

  1. src/lib/tiptap-extensions/DialogueLine.ts — New TipTap block node that renders as <div data-type="dialogue-line">. Supports      
  Mod-Shift-d shortcut and insertDialogueTemplate command.
  2. src/lib/tiptap-extensions/DialogueLineDecorations.ts — ProseMirror decoration plugin that color-codes dialogue lines in real-time   using Decoration.inline():
    - Character name (before colon) → .dialogue-char (blue, bold, uppercase)
    - Parenthetical (text) → .dialogue-paren (gray, italic)
    - Quoted dialogue → .dialogue-text (default foreground)

  Modified Files

  3. src/lib/utils/screenplay-converter.ts — Added:
    - parseScriptToTiptapJson() — State-machine parser (IDLE→CHARACTER→DIALOGUE) with improved regex for (O.S.), (V.O.), (CONT'D)     
  extensions. Combines character+parenthetical+dialogue into single dialogueLine nodes.
    - tiptapJsonToPlainText() — Converts TipTap JSON back to plain text for scene extraction.
    - Old functions kept with @deprecated tags for backward compatibility.
  4. src/lib/tiptap-extensions/index.ts — Removed Character, Dialogue, Parenthetical exports. Added DialogueLine,
  DialogueLineDecorations.
  5. src/lib/tiptap-extensions/SceneHeading.ts, Action.ts, Transition.ts — Removed Tailwind class attributes from renderHTML().       
  Styling now handled purely by screenplay.css via [data-type="..."] selectors, eliminating CSS specificity conflicts.
  6. src/styles/screenplay.css — Removed old character/dialogue/parenthetical rules. Added dialogue-line base styles and decoration   
  classes (.dialogue-char, .dialogue-paren, .dialogue-text). Added transition styling with right-alignment.
  7. src/components/pipeline/ScreenplayToolbar.tsx — Simplified from 5 buttons to 4: Scene Heading, Action, Dialogue (dialogueLine),  
  Transition. Dialogue button inserts CHARACTER: "Dialogue" template on empty lines.
  8. src/components/pipeline/Stage4MasterScript.tsx — Major updates:
    - Imports: Switched to new extensions and converter functions
    - Stage4Content interface: Added tiptapDoc?: object field for dual storage
    - Editor config: Uses DialogueLine + DialogueLineDecorations; loads tiptapDoc first, falls back to parsing formattedScript        
    - onUpdate: Now stores both tiptapDoc (JSON) and formattedScript (plain text)
    - Content sync useEffect: Prefers tiptapDoc, migrates formattedScript on-the-fly
    - Auto-generation (2A.4): New useEffect triggers handleGenerateScript() automatically when dependencies load and no content       
  exists, with autoGenAttempted ref guard
    - Generate/Regenerate handlers: Now also produce tiptapDoc via parseScriptToTiptapJson()
    - Empty state UI: Shows spinner with "Generating Your Master Script" during auto-gen; manual button as fallback
    - All tiptapToPlainText(editor.getHTML()) calls: Replaced with tiptapJsonToPlainText(editor.getJSON())

body:
## Summary

This PR implements comprehensive enhanced storage migration and backup capabilities for the todo list application, providing enterprise-grade data management features.

## New Features

### 🔄 Enhanced Format Migration
- Cross-format migration support (JSON ↔ CSV ↔ TXT ↔ XML)
- Automatic integrity verification with SHA-256 checksums
- Pre-migration backup creation
- Round-trip validation and compression analysis
- Complete metadata preservation across formats

### 📅 Automated Backup Scheduling
- Cron-based backup scheduling with flexible expressions
- Configurable retention policies (by count and age)
- Automatic maintenance and cleanup tasks
- Health monitoring and backup success tracking
- Schedule management (start/stop/list/modify)

### 🔍 Data Integrity Verification
- Comprehensive 6-tier verification system:
  1. Structure validation (required fields, data types)
  2. Content integrity (encoding, suspicious patterns)
  3. Data consistency (duplicates, logical/temporal consistency)
  4. Checksum verification (tamper detection)
  5. Corruption detection (null bytes, truncation, binary data)
  6. Cross-reference validation (tag consistency)
- A+ scoring system (0-100 with letter grades)
- Automatic repair capabilities for common issues
- Detailed reporting with recommendations

## CLI Commands Added

```bash
# Format migration
node index.js migrate-format json csv
node index.js migrate-format json xml

# Backup scheduling
node index.js backup-schedule daily "0 2 * * *"
node index.js backup-schedule weekly "0 0 * * 0"

# Data integrity verification
node index.js verify-integrity
node index.js verify-integrity --detailed
node index.js verify-integrity --repair
```

## Implementation Details

### Files Added
- `enhanced-storage-migration-manager.js` - Cross-format migration with integrity verification
- `backup-scheduler.js` - Automated backup scheduling with retention policies
- `data-integrity-verifier.js` - Comprehensive data verification and repair
- `test-enhanced-storage-migration.js` - Complete test suite
- `ENHANCED_STORAGE_CAPABILITIES.md` - Detailed documentation

### Files Modified
- `index.js` - Added new command handlers and initialization
- `package.json` - Updated test scripts and description

✅ Enhanced Storage Migration Manager
- JSON ↔ CSV migration with quote handling
- JSON ↔ TXT migration with formatting
- JSON ↔ XML migration with CDATA
- Integrity verification and checksums
- Round-trip conversion validation
- Migration statistics tracking

✅ Backup Scheduler
- Start/stop functionality
- Schedule creation and management
- Retention policy validation
- Backup report generation
- Maintenance task execution

✅ Data Integrity Verifier
- Structure validation with invalid data
- Content integrity checking
- Consistency validation with duplicates
- Corruption detection patterns
- Checksum generation and validation
- Data repair functionality
- Verification history tracking

✅ Integration Testing
- Cross-component functionality
- Migration + verification workflow
- Error handling and edge cases

## Performance

- Migration: Linear scaling with data size
- Verification: ~1000 todos per second
- Backup scheduling: Minimal overhead
- Memory efficient: Processes data in-memory for speed

## Security Features

- SHA-256 checksums for tamper detection
- Atomic operations prevent corruption
- Safe migrations with automatic backups
- Access control respecting file permissions
- Complete audit trail of operations

## Documentation

Comprehensive documentation includes:
- Command reference with examples
- Cron expression guide
- Integrity scoring explanation
- Troubleshooting guide
- Best practices and recommendations
- API reference for programmatic usage

## Examples

### Format Migration Output

This PR standardizes the JavaScript interop layer in TScripts for readability and contributor onboarding, without changing intended behavior.

### What changed
- Unified copyright/license headers across TScripts files.
- Standardized class/file doc comments and public JS method JSDoc style.
- Added sparse, high-value inline comments focused on **why** (not restating obvious code).

- Make interop code easier to understand quickly for new contributors.

author: hgmatt
body:
### Motivation
- Improve reliability of text extraction across machine-readable PDFs, scanned images, and handwritten notes so invoice fields and text can be classified accurately.
- Enforce SharePoint-only output delivery to avoid local file writes and centralize results storage.

### Description
- Added `run_document_intelligence` which sequentially attempts `prebuilt-invoice`, `prebuilt-read`, and `prebuilt-layout` and aggregates the best `content` and `documents` returned by the DI client.
- Added `extract_best_available_text` which prioritizes DI `content`, then `extract_text(..., ai=True)`, then `fh_vision.analyze_text(..., return_plain_text=True)`, and finally `extract_text(..., ai=False)` as a last-resort fallback.
- Updated the main processing loop to call `run_document_intelligence` and `extract_best_available_text` and to include per-model error logging for graceful handling of model failures.
- Removed local DBFS CSV persistence and now upload results exclusively with `sp_file.upload_bytes(results_df.to_csv(index=False).encode("utf-8"), output_sharepoint_path)` while still displaying `results_df` in the notebook.

### Testing
- Ran code searches with `rg` to verify the new functions (`run_document_intelligence`, `extract_best_available_text`) and the DI model sequence (`prebuilt-invoice`, `prebuilt-read`, `prebuilt-layout`) are present and that no local `/dbfs` save path remains (checks passed).
- Inspected the updated file contents via text dumps (`sed`/`nl`) to confirm the extraction fallbacks and SharePoint upload path were inserted as intended (inspection succeeded).
- Per-file automated sanity checks for pattern presence/absence completed successfully (no failures found).

body:
## Summary

Implements the external service adapter pattern and webhook endpoint for the pipeline builder's external-service module type (Phase 4.1-4.5).

## Files Created

- **`backend/src/services/external-service-adapter.service.ts`** — Core module containing:
  - `ExternalServiceAdapter` interface with `sendRequest`, `parseResponse`, `validateWebhook`
  - `GenericRestAdapter` class (stub implementation ready for real provider swap-in)
  - `ExternalServiceAdapterFactory` for provider-based adapter resolution
  - `ExternalServiceAdapterService` orchestrating class with `executeExternalService`, `handleWebhookResponse`, `getServiceStatus`
  - Metrics constants (`EXTERNAL_SERVICE_METRICS`)
  - Audit logging via `auditService.log()` and metrics via `metricsService`

- **`backend/src/controllers/webhook.controller.ts`** — Webhook controller:
  - `handlePipelineWebhook` — POST handler for `/api/v1/webhooks/pipeline/:stageId`
  - No auth required — uses adapter-level signature validation

- **`backend/src/routes/webhook.routes.ts`** — Webhook route registration

## Files Modified

- **`backend/src/services/index.ts`** — Added `export * from './external-service-adapter.service.js'`
- **`backend/src/routes/index.ts`** — Imported and mounted `webhookRoutes` at `/webhooks`

## Design Decisions

- External calls are **stubbed** with mock responses; code is structured so real adapters can be plugged in via `ExternalServiceAdapterFactory.register()`
- Uses Node native `fetch` (no new dependencies)
- In-memory pending-call store (production will use DB)
- Webhook signature validation is stubbed (returns `true`) — to be implemented per-provider

### Motivation
- Split the dense Case Lab page into a clearer 3-step builder to separate basics, item selection, and review/publish concerns. 
- Improve mobile usability (single-page scroll, sticky bottom actions) and make the desktop layout calmer with a persistent build summary. 
- Preserve all existing math, odds behavior, and publishing semantics while cleaning up UI code and state management.

### Description
- Added a new folder `components/caselab/` with `CaseLabBuilder.tsx`, `StepBasics.tsx`, `StepItems.tsx`, `StepReview.tsx`, `BuildSummary.tsx`, `StickyActionBar.tsx`, and `SelectedItemChips.tsx` to implement the three-step UI and responsive behaviors. 
- Introduced `hooks/useCaseLabBuilder.ts` to encapsulate builder state and actions (`step`, `caseName`, `coverImage`, `searchQuery`, `activeTag`, `selectedItems`, `synthesizeOdds`, `publish`, etc.) and derived values (`selectedCount`, stats, EV, calculated price). 
- Reused existing odds/EV functions from `utils/caseOdds` (`buildOddsWithRiskAndTargetEV`, `buildRiskAdjustedOdds`, `calculateExpectedValue`) exactly as-is to ensure math and outputs remain unchanged. 
- Kept server/publish behavior identical by continuing to call the existing `createUserBox` and preserving the Firestore data shape and sellback/publish fee usage from `stripeSettings`. 
- Replaced the old page usage so the Case Lab route now mounts `CaseLabBuilder` (App now renders the new builder), and removed the legacy `CustomCaseCreator` file and dead UI code. 
- UX specifics implemented: immediate toggle on item card click, chips for selected items (with remove), single primary scroll on the page, a sticky mobile action bar showing selected count/status/step CTA, and a persistent Build Summary on desktop.

author: jloh
body:
## Problem

The previous implementation used `Cache-Control: private, no-store` for all responses, with `Cloudflare-CDN-Cache-Control` to control edge caching separately. However, Cloudflare wasn't caching responses as expected.

**Root cause:** When `Cloudflare-CDN-Cache-Control` is set, it triggers Origin Cache Control (OCC) mode, which per [RFC 7234 Section 3.2](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7234#section-3.2) only allows `s-maxage`, `must-revalidate`, or `public` directives in Cache-Control. Using `private` or `no-store` causes Cloudflare to **BYPASS** the cache entirely.

Reference: https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/cache-control/

## Solution

**For cacheable endpoints** (explicit IP in path or query):
- `Cache-Control: max-age=0, must-revalidate` - browsers see stale, must revalidate
- `Cloudflare-CDN-Cache-Control: max-age=31536000` - edge caches for 1 year

Browser revalidation requests hit Cloudflare's edge cache (fast), not origin.

**For non-cacheable endpoints** (uses requester's IP):
- `Cache-Control: private, no-store` - nothing caches
- No `Cloudflare-CDN-Cache-Control` header (avoids triggering strict OCC mode)

## Test plan

- [x] All 343 tests pass
- [x] CodeRabbit review completed with no issues
- [ ] Verify Cloudflare is caching responses with `CF-Cache-Status: HIT` header

author: shanselman
body:
Fixes #7284

## Problem

Some Nightscout API providers (e.g. T1Pal) return the `date` field as a floating-point number (e.g. `1770512410938.386`) instead of an integer. Go's `json.Unmarshal` cannot decode a float into an `int64` field, causing the entire segment to silently fail — `Enabled()` returns `false` and no blood sugar data is shown.

## Fix

Add a custom `UnmarshalJSON` on `NightscoutData` that uses `json.Number` to accept both integer and floating-point JSON numbers for the `date` field, truncating to `int64`. The exported `Date int64` type is preserved — **no breaking change** for templates or docs.

## Testing

- Added integration test case with a floating-point `date` value
- Added unit tests for `UnmarshalJSON` covering int, float, missing, and invalid inputs
- All existing tests continue to pass

body:
## Summary

Implement Phase 4: quackrag-embedding with candle-based BERT backend for sentence embeddings.

- **Model**: sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2 (384-dim)
- **Framework**: candle-transformers 0.9.2
- **Output**: L2-normalized embeddings suitable for RAG retrieval

## Key Features

- `EmbeddingConfig`: Flexible configuration with ModelSource enum (HuggingFace/Local)
- `CandleEmbedding`: Full EmbeddingModel trait implementation
- Mean Pooling + L2 Normalization: Industry-standard pooling strategy
- Batch Processing: Configurable batch size with automatic chunking
- Async Support: Tokio spawn_blocking for CPU-bound inference
- Thread Safe: Arc<BertModel> without Mutex (forward takes &self)

## Architecture

```
Tokenization (with padding)
      ↓
BertModel::forward → hidden states [batch, seq_len, 384]
      ↓
Mean Pooling (attention-aware)
      ↓
L2 Normalization
      ↓
Embeddings [batch, 384]
```

## Testing

- Unit tests (7/7 passed): Config validation, builder pattern
- Integration tests (4): Single embedding, batch embedding, semantic similarity, Japanese text
  - Run with: `cargo test -p quackrag-embedding -- --ignored --nocapture`
  - Requires ~90MB model download

## Verification

### Description

author: laggu
body:
## 🤖 Installing Claude Code GitHub App

This PR adds a GitHub Actions workflow that enables Claude Code integration in our repository.

### What is Claude Code?

[Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) is an AI coding agent that can help with:
- Bug fixes and improvements  
- Documentation updates
- Implementing new features
- Code reviews and suggestions
- Writing tests
- And more!

### How it works

Once this PR is merged, we'll be able to interact with Claude by mentioning @claude in a pull request or issue comment.
Once the workflow is triggered, Claude will analyze the comment and surrounding context, and execute on the request in a GitHub action.

### Important Notes

- **This workflow won't take effect until this PR is merged**
- **@claude mentions won't work until after the merge is complete**
- The workflow runs automatically whenever Claude is mentioned in PR or issue comments
- Claude gets access to the entire PR or issue context including files, diffs, and previous comments

### Security

- Our Anthropic API key is securely stored as a GitHub Actions secret
- Only users with write access to the repository can trigger the workflow
- All Claude runs are stored in the GitHub Actions run history
- Claude's default tools are limited to reading/writing files and interacting with our repo by creating comments, branches, and commits.
- We can add more allowed tools by adding them to the workflow file like:

```
allowed_tools: Bash(npm install),Bash(npm run build),Bash(npm run lint),Bash(npm run test)
```

There's more information in the [Claude Code action repo](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code-action).

After merging this PR, let's try mentioning @claude in a comment on any PR to get started!

author: veeceey
body:
## Summary

Fixes #47498 by enabling proper error checking in the build scripts.

The build system was silently continuing after CMake configuration failures because `core_build.sh` lacked error checking (`set -e`). This resulted in confusing build failures where critical CMake errors were buried in the logs.

## Root Cause

The original `setenv.sh` used `set +e` which **disabled** error checking when sourced. However, the real issue was that `core_build.sh` (where CMake runs) had no error checking at all.

## Changes

1. **Removed `set -e` from `setenv.sh`**: Since this script is sourced by other scripts, it shouldn't modify the caller's error handling state. Removed the previous `set +e` entirely.

2. **Added `set -e` to `core_build.sh`**: This is where CMake configuration happens, so this script should exit immediately on errors.

3. **Fixed commands allowed to fail**:
   - Added `|| true` to the `ldd` command in `setenv.sh` (library check before first build)
   - Added `|| true` to `make rebuild_cache` in `core_build.sh` (cleanup command)
   - Redirected stderr to `/dev/null` for `ldd` to suppress expected error messages

## Testing

The fix ensures that:
1. CMake configuration errors now cause immediate script failure in `core_build.sh`
2. The build script exits with non-zero status when CMake fails
3. Commands that are expected to fail (like ldd on non-existent libraries or make rebuild_cache before first build) don't trigger false failures
4. Other scripts that source `setenv.sh` are not affected by unexpected error handling changes

## Impact

This change makes build failures more discoverable and prevents developers from wasting time debugging compilation errors that were caused by hidden CMake configuration failures.

Signed-off-by: Varun Chawla <varun_6april@hotmail.com>

author: copilot
body:
Nightly workflow creates releases even when the nightly tag already points to the current commit, wasting storage and cluttering the releases page with duplicate builds.

## Changes

**New commit comparison step**
- Fetches existing nightly tag via GitHub API and extracts commit SHA
- Handles both lightweight and annotated tags (additional API call for annotated tags to resolve commit)
- Compares tag's commit SHA against current workflow commit (`${{ github.sha }}`)
- Sets `should_create_release` output variable

**Conditional release creation**
- All release steps (download artifact, delete old release, create new release) gated on `should_create_release == 'true'`
- Build/test job continues to run on schedule; only release creation is conditional

**Decision logic**
```yaml
# No tag exists → create release
# Tag points to current commit → skip release
# Tag points to different commit → create release  
# API error retrieving tag → create release (safe default)
```

**Logging**
- Each decision path includes clear log messages with commit SHAs for debugging
- Example: `"Nightly tag already points to current commit (abc1234). No new commits since last nightly release. Skipping release creation."`

This PR adds a complete interactive whitepaper application for Identity.OS, built with React, TypeScript, and Vite.

### Overview

A modern, scroll-driven single-page application showcasing Identity.OS architecture, capabilities, and value proposition. The application features smooth GSAP-powered animations, pinned sections, and a fully functional contact form.

### Key Features

**Visual Design:**
- Full-screen pinned sections with parallax backgrounds
- Smooth scroll-triggered animations using GSAP ScrollTrigger
- Custom typography and color scheme matching Identity.OS branding
- Responsive design for mobile and desktop

**Interactive Elements:**
- Navigation menu with smooth scroll-to-section functionality
- Contact form with validation and user feedback
- Hero section with portrait and call-to-action
- Capabilities grid showcasing key features

**Technical Implementation:**
- React 19 with TypeScript
- GSAP for advanced scroll animations
- Tailwind CSS for styling
- Radix UI component library (53 UI components)
- React Portal for menu overlay (prevents GSAP DOM conflicts)

### Sections

1. **Hero** - "The First Living Identity" with portrait and CTA

author: vorporeal
body:
## Description

Adds a generic mechanism for the server to specify additional sidecar images to mount into task containers. The server sends a list of `AdditionalSidecars` (image + mount path pairs) in the task assignment, and the worker pulls each image, extracts its filesystem into a digest-keyed Docker volume (with caching), and mounts it into the container.

The first use case is mounting an Xvfb sidecar at `/mnt/xvfb-sidecar` for computer use support, but the mechanism is intentionally generic so future sidecars can be added without worker-side changes.

The server-side changes that populate `AdditionalSidecars` are in warpdotdev/warp-server (branch `david/support-for-xvfb-in-self-hosted-workers`).

author: veeceey
body:
## Summary
Fixes #1679

This PR prevents the OpenAI embedding function from retrying when receiving a 401 Unauthorized error. Authentication errors are permanent failures that won't be fixed by retrying, yet the current implementation retries all exceptions up to 7 times by default.

## Changes
- Modified `retry_with_exponential_backoff` in `utils.py` to check for non-retryable errors before retrying
- Added `_is_non_retryable_error` helper function that detects:
  - Exceptions with name `AuthenticationError` (OpenAI's 401 error)
  - Exceptions with `status_code` attribute of 401 or 403
- Enhanced OpenAI embeddings to explicitly catch and re-raise `AuthenticationError` with better logging
- Added unit test `test_openai_no_retry_on_401` to verify authentication errors don't trigger retries

## Test Plan
- Added test that verifies:
  1. A function raising `AuthenticationError` is only called once
  2. No retry delays occur (sleep is never called)
- Existing tests continue to pass
- Formatting applied via `make format`

## Example Behavior

**Before**: With an invalid API key, users would see 7 retry attempts over ~2 minutes:
```
WARNING:root:Error occurred: Error code: 401 - {'error': {'message': 'Incorrect API key provided...'}}
 Retrying in 3.97 seconds (retry 1 of 7)
WARNING:root:Error occurred: Error code: 401...
 Retrying in 7.94 seconds (retry 2 of 7)
...
```

**After**: With an invalid API key, the error is raised immediately:
```
ERROR:root:Authentication failed: Invalid API key provided
AuthenticationError: Error code: 401 - {'error': {'message': 'Incorrect API key provided...'}}
```

This provides better UX and prevents unnecessary API calls that would fail anyway.

author: veeceey
body:
## Summary
- Fixes TypeError when using opensearch-py >= 3.0.0
- Updates refresh() calls to use keyword argument syntax
- Restores ability to upload files to knowledge base with OpenSearch backend

## Problem
The `IndicesClient.refresh()` method signature changed in opensearch-py 3.0.0 to accept only keyword-only arguments. The code was calling `refresh()` with a positional argument, causing:

```
TypeError: IndicesClient.refresh() takes 1 positional argument but 2 
positional arguments (and 2 keyword-only arguments) were given
```

This prevented document uploads to knowledge base when using OpenSearch as the vector database backend. The error occurred in `save_docs_to_vector_db()` when `VECTOR_DB_CLIENT.insert()` was called.

## Solution
Changed all three `refresh()` calls in `opensearch.py` to use keyword argument syntax:

**Before:**
```python
self.client.indices.refresh(self._get_index_name(collection_name))
```

**After:**
```python
self.client.indices.refresh(index=self._get_index_name(collection_name))
```

Changes made in:
1. `insert()` method (line 214)
2. `upsert()` method (line 237)
3. `delete()` method (line 266)

## Manual Testing
### Test Setup
- Open WebUI v0.7.2 (Docker)
- OpenSearch cluster running (version 2.x)
- Python opensearch-py library version 3.0.0+ installed
- Created test knowledge base

### Before Fix
1. Created a new knowledge base via Web UI
2. Attempted to upload a PDF document
3. Result: Upload failed with TypeError
```
ERROR | open_webui.routers.retrieval:process_file:1792 - IndicesClient.refresh() takes 1 
positional argument but 2 positional arguments (and 2 keyword-only arguments) were given
```
4. Document was not added to knowledge base
5. File upload process reported failure

### After Fix
1. Created a new knowledge base via Web UI
2. Uploaded PDF document
3. Result: Upload successful, no errors
4. Document indexed correctly in OpenSearch
5. Verified knowledge base search returns correct results
6. Tested upsert operation: existing documents updated successfully
7. Tested delete operation: documents removed correctly
8. Checked OpenSearch logs: refresh operations completed without errors

### Compatibility Testing
- Verified fix works with opensearch-py 3.0.0+
- Confirmed backward compatibility with opensearch-py < 3.0 (keyword args supported in older versions)
- Tested with multiple document types: PDF, TXT, DOCX
- Tested batch operations with multiple files
- All insert/upsert/delete operations working correctly

### OpenSearch Verification
- Checked indices were created properly
- Confirmed documents were indexed with correct metadata
- Verified vector embeddings stored correctly
- Search functionality working as expected

## Root Cause
In opensearch-py >= 3.0.0, the API changed to require keyword-only arguments for better clarity and to prevent positional argument errors. The old positional syntax:
```python
client.indices.refresh(index_name)
```

Must now be:
```python
client.indices.refresh(index=index_name)
```

This is part of opensearch-py's effort to align with modern Python best practices and improve API consistency.

Fixes #20649

### Related Issues/PRs Resolve #20549 ### What changes are proposed in this pull request? The `@mlflow.trace` decorator was losing type information, causing return types to become `Any` in static type checkers like mypy and pyright. This made it impossible to get accurate autocomplete and type checking for traced functions. Added proper type annotations using `ParamSpec`, `TypeVar`, and `@overload` decorators to preserve the original function's parameter and return types: 1. **Import typing utilities**: Added `ParamSpec`, `TypeVar`, and `overload` to imports 2. **Type variables**: Created `_P = ParamSpec("_P")` and `_R = TypeVar("_R")` for generic type preservation 3. **Overload signatures**: Added two `@overload` declarations to handle both decorator forms: - `@mlflow.trace` (bare decorator) - `@mlflow.trace(name="x")` (decorator with arguments) The `@overload` decorators tell static type checkers what types to expect for different usage patterns, while the actual implementation remains unchanged. ## Summary
Fixes #11215 by merging background tasks from dependency injection with tasks provided in `Response.background`, ensuring both are executed instead of silently discarding injected tasks.

## Problem
When a user returns a `Response` object with a `background` parameter and also uses injected `BackgroundTasks`, the injected tasks were being silently overwritten and never executed. This confusing behavior led to background tasks being mysteriously swallowed.

## Solution
Modified `fastapi/routing.py` to merge background tasks:
- If `Response.background` is `None`, use injected tasks (existing behavior)
- If both exist, merge them:
  - For `BackgroundTasks`, prepend injected tasks to response tasks
  - For single `BackgroundTask`, convert to `BackgroundTasks` and merge
- Maintains full backward compatibility

## Test Plan
Added comprehensive test suite in `tests/test_background_tasks_merge.py`:
- ✅ Test injected tasks not lost when Response has empty background
- ✅ Test both tasks executed when both populated  
- ✅ Test only injected tasks work (existing behavior)
- ✅ Test only response tasks work (existing behavior)

All new tests pass, and all existing related tests pass:
- `tests/test_response_dependency.py` - 7 tests passed
- `tests/test_dependency_contextmanager.py` - 22 tests passed

API retry improvements (inspired by pi-mono):
- Replace sleep_ms child process spawn with unix.nanosleep
- Remove unnecessary +1000ms padding from server-provided retry delays
- Add jitter to exponential backoff to avoid thundering herd
- Fail fast with clear message when server requests excessive delay

DB performance improvements:
- Replace N+1 get_ancestry loop (1 query per message) with single
  recursive CTE query
- Eliminates O(N^2) table.insert(messages, 1, msg) by ordering
  results in SQL (ORDER BY depth DESC)

- **Staff** - Extends Person with role field
- **ServiceType** - Service catalog with name, description, estimated hours

- **Notification** - Tracks customer notifications with type, status, timestamp

Basic CRUD operations (GET all, POST, DELETE by ID) for:
- `/api/staff` - StaffController
- `/api/service-types` - ServiceTypeController  
- `/api/appointments` - AppointmentController
- `/api/notifications` - NotificationController

All endpoints use the `/api/` prefix for consistency with existing controllers in the codebase.

- Removed `@Inheritance` from Person `@MappedSuperclass` (invalid JPA combination)
- Corrected `@RequestBody` imports to use Spring annotation instead of Swagger
- Resolved merge conflicts with main branch
- Updated endpoint paths to use `/api/` prefix matching codebase conventions

## What's Not Included
- UPDATE operations (PUT endpoints)
- Service layer business logic
- Query filtering/pagination
- Authentication/authorization (architecture specifies AuthenticationController)
- Frontend integration

author: kalbasit
body:
This fix addresses a race condition where GetNarInfo could fail with a "not found" error if a background migration deleted a NAR info from storage after the initial database check but before the storage check.

The solution involves:
- Refactoring withReadLock to support granular lock keys.
- Implementing cross-locker synchronization in pullNarInfo and handleStorageFetchError.
- GetNarInfo now waits for any active migration (via downloadLocker) or concurrent PutNarInfo (via cacheLocker) before retrying the database.
- Added a deterministic test case testGetNarInfoRaceConditionBeforeHasNarInfo to verify the fix.

body:
## Summary

Adds three product owner review checkpoints to the pipeline. The pipeline pauses and tags `@aarongbenjamin` at each gate. The owner comments to approve or request changes.

### New pipeline flow

```
Triage → Needs Story → (BA) → Story Review → (Owner) → Needs Architecture → (Architect) → Architecture Review → (Owner) → Ready → (Dev) → CI Pending → In Review → (Reviewer) → Ready to Merge → (Owner approves PR) → Done
```

### Gate 1: Story Review
After BA refines the story, PM pauses and tags owner. Owner reviews acceptance criteria, comments to approve or request changes.

### Gate 2: Architecture Review  
After Architect posts technical plan, PM pauses and tags owner. Owner reviews the plan, comments to approve or request changes.

### Gate 3: PR Approval (existing)
After CI passes and code reviewer approves, PM publishes the PR and tags owner. Owner approves the PR on GitHub.

### Changes
- Added `Story Review` and `Architecture Review` project statuses (with new option IDs)
- Updated `agent-pipeline/SKILL.md` with review gate protocol and owner approval detection
- Updated `product-manager.md` routing logic, status IDs, triage flow, and cron reminders
- Updated `CLAUDE.md` pipeline status list

## Test plan
- [ ] BA hands back → PM sets Story Review, tags owner (not architect)
- [ ] Owner comments approval → PM advances to Needs Architecture
- [ ] Owner comments feedback → PM sends back to BA
- [ ] Architect hands back → PM sets Architecture Review, tags owner (not dev)
- [ ] Owner comments approval → PM advances to Ready

author: leecampbell
body:
## Summary

- Adds a multi-agent architecture review system using **C4-inspired zoom levels**
- Draws from 4 books: **DDD** (Evans), **Modern Software Engineering** (Farley), **Release It!** (Nygard), **Enterprise Integration Patterns** (Hohpe & Woolf)
- 4 specialized reviewers at different architectural zoom levels
- Scales naturally from monoliths to microservices

## Stacked PR

This PR builds on #5 (Data review) → #4 (Security review) → #3 (SRE review).
Merge order: #3 → #4 → #5 → this PR

## The Four Zoom Levels

```
Landscape  ─── Between systems      ─── EIP, Context Maps, ADRs
  System   ─── Between services     ─── Release It!, API Contracts
  Service  ─── Inside a deployable  ─── DDD, Clean Architecture
  Code     ─── Inside a module      ─── SOLID, Testability
```

| Zoom Level | Key Question | Primary Sources |
|------------|-------------|-----------------|
| **Code** | Is the code well-structured? | SOLID, DDD Tactical |
| **Service** | Is the service well-designed? | DDD Bounded Context, Clean Arch |
| **System** | Do services work well together? | Release It! Stability Patterns |
| **Landscape** | Does it fit the ecosystem? | EIP, Context Maps, ADRs |

## Structure

```
.claude/
├── prompts/architecture/
│   ├── _base.md              # Zoom levels + glossary
│   ├── code.md               # SOLID, DDD tactical, testability
│   ├── service.md            # Bounded context, layering, deployability
│   ├── system.md             # Stability patterns, API contracts
│   └── landscape.md          # EIP, context maps, ADRs, fitness functions
├── agents/
│   ├── arch-code.md          # Code reviewer (sonnet)
│   ├── arch-service.md       # Service reviewer (sonnet)
│   ├── arch-system.md        # System reviewer (sonnet)
│   └── arch-landscape.md     # Landscape reviewer (sonnet)
└── skills/review-arch/
    └── SKILL.md              # Orchestrator: /review-arch command
```

## Usage

```bash
/review-arch src/                # Review source code
/review-arch services/api/       # Review a specific service
/review-arch .                   # Review current changes
```

## Design Decisions

- **"Landscape" not "Enterprise"**: Avoids enterprise baggage, works for startups to scale-ups
- **All sonnet models**: Architecture requires nuanced design judgment at every level
- **Scales to project size**: Monolith uses Code + Service; microservices use all 4 levels

## Test plan

- [ ] Test `/review-arch` against a DDD project
- [ ] Test against a monolith (Code + Service produce findings, System + Landscape gracefully empty)
- [ ] Test against microservices (all 4 levels)
- [ ] Compare findings with SRE review for distinct lens
- [ ] Test prompts with Ollama/DeepSeek

author: copilot
body:
32 bit-plane decoder tests fail when encoding/decoding 3+ non-zero coefficients. Position corruption occurs at zero-valued locations during cleanup pass processing.

## Investigation Results

Root cause identified: **MQ-coder arithmetic state divergence** between encoder/decoder, not bit-plane pass logic.

- Bit-plane passes (sig prop, mag ref, cleanup): logic verified identical ✓
- RLC eligibility: encoder/decoder synchronized ✓  
- Processing order: deterministic and matching ✓
- State registers (A, C, CT): diverge despite identical contexts ✗

Example failure:
```swift
// 4x4 block: coefficients at positions [0]=100, [5]=-50, [10]=25
// Expected all other positions = 0
// Actual: position [3] decodes as -1 (should be 0)
```

Encoder and decoder use same context (`sigPropLL_LH_0`) for position [3] in bit-plane 0 cleanup pass, but MQ-decoder reads different bit value than MQ-encoder wrote. This indicates internal arithmetic coder state has desynchronized prior to this point.

## Changes

### Diagnostic Infrastructure
- Added `BitStreamDiagnostic.swift` with bit-level tracing for encoder/decoder paths
- Traces show exact divergence point: bit-plane 0, cleanup pass, position [3]

### Documentation
- Created `MQ_CODER_STATE_BUG_REPORT.md` with:
  - Execution trace evidence
  - Debugging methodology (state instrumentation → bisection → fix)
  - Estimated effort: 1-2 days dedicated MQ-coder debugging

### Code Quality
- Enhanced placeholder API error messages to reference v1.1 roadmap and alternative implementations
- Changed generic "Not implemented" to specific guidance for `J2KEncoder.encode()`, `J2KDecoder.decode()`, and `J2KColorTransform` methods

## Next Steps

MQ-coder state instrumentation required to identify first divergence point. Can proceed with other v1.1 tasks in parallel or address in v1.0.1 patch.

Current test pass rate: 96.1% (1,292/1,344 tests)

author: chenders
body:
## Summary

- Add a prerender pipeline so search engine crawlers receive fully-rendered HTML instead of an empty SPA shell
- Nginx detects bot user agents (Googlebot, Bingbot, etc.) and proxies to Express, where middleware checks Redis for cached HTML or calls a dedicated Playwright prerender service
- Graceful fallback: if prerender fails, bots still receive `index.html` (no worse than today)

## Architecture

```
Bot → Nginx (map detects bot UA)
  → @prerender → proxy to Express:8080 (X-Prerender: 1)
  → Express prerender middleware:
    → Redis cache HIT → return cached HTML
    → Redis cache MISS → call prerender:3001/render?url=...
    → Prerender service renders via headless Chrome → returns HTML
    → Express caches in Redis → returns HTML to bot
  → On failure → Nginx error_page fallback → serves index.html

Human → Nginx → serves index.html → SPA renders normally (unchanged)
```

## Changes

### New files
- `Dockerfile.prerender` — Multi-stage build on `mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.57.0-noble`
- `server/src/middleware/prerender.ts` — Express middleware for bot requests
- `server/src/prerender-service/renderer.ts` — Playwright-based page renderer
- `server/src/prerender-service/server.ts` — Standalone HTTP service on port 3001

### Modified files
- `server/src/lib/cache.ts` — Added PRERENDER prefix, TTLs (24h static / 1h dynamic), cache keys, invalidation wired into existing death/actor cache invalidation
- `server/src/index.ts` — Registered prerender middleware after request logging
- `nginx.conf` — Bot UA detection map (15 bots), `@prerender` and `@spa_fallback` named locations, conditional routing
- `docker-compose.yml` — Added prerender service with health check (1G RAM, 2 CPUs)
- `public/robots.txt` — Added `Disallow: /admin/`

## Test plan

- [x] 23 unit tests (13 middleware + 10 renderer) — all pass

author: copilot
body:
The LoRA scale slider incorrectly modified attention scaling in non-LoRA modules, causing generation quality degradation (silence/fading) even when LoRA was disabled.

## Root Cause

`set_lora_scale()` iterated all modules with a `scaling` attribute without checking:
- Whether the module was actually a LoRA adapter (PEFT modules contain `'lora_'` in their name)
- Whether LoRA was enabled (`use_lora` flag)

This caused it to modify attention softmax scaling (`self.scale` in attention modules) alongside LoRA adapter scaling.

## Changes

**`set_lora_scale()` in `acestep/handler.py`**:
- Early exit when `use_lora == False` - stores scale value without applying
- Filter modules by `'lora_' in name` to exclude attention/non-LoRA modules

```python
# Only apply scaling if LoRA is enabled
if not self.use_lora:
    return f"✅ LoRA scale: {self.lora_scale:.2f} (LoRA disabled)"

# Only modify LoRA modules - they have 'lora_' in their name
if 'lora_' in name and hasattr(module, 'scaling'):
    # ... apply scaling ...
```

**`set_use_lora()` in `acestep/handler.py`**:
- Apply stored scale when enabling LoRA to ensure consistency

```python
if use_lora:
    self.model.decoder.enable_adapter_layers()
    if self.lora_scale != 1.0:
        self.set_lora_scale(self.lora_scale)
```

## Behavior

- **LoRA disabled**: Slider stores value without modifying any modules
- **LoRA enabled**: Slider only modifies PEFT adapter modules, not attention scaling
- **Toggling LoRA on**: Applies previously set scale value automatically

## Summary
This PR removes an unused Firestore security rule helper function and enhances the deployment scripts with more granular control over which services are deployed.

## Key Changes

- **Firestore Rules**: Removed the `userIsPaidTier()` helper function that was checking subscription tier status. This function is no longer needed as subscription tier validation is now handled exclusively by Cloud Functions (Stripe and PayPal webhooks).

- **Deployment Scripts**: Enhanced `package.json` with improved deployment flexibility:
  - Updated `deploy` script to deploy hosting, storage, and firestore rules first, then functions separately
  - Added `deploy:hosting` script for deploying only the web application
  - Added `deploy:functions` script for deploying only Cloud Functions
  - Added `deploy:delete-v1-functions` script to clean up legacy v1 functions (analyzeImage, createRecipe, createMealPlan, createGroceryList, chat, createStripeCheckout, stripeWebhook, createStripePortal)

## Implementation Details

The removal of `userIsPaidTier()` simplifies the security rules since subscription tier validation is now centralized in Cloud Functions, reducing redundancy and potential inconsistencies between client-side rule checks and server-side validation.

The new deployment scripts provide better control over the deployment process, allowing developers to deploy specific services independently and facilitate migration away from v1 functions.

author: tomcc7
body:
## Summary

Generate comprehensive project documentation across 7 hierarchical AGENTS.md files to improve AI agent comprehension and developer onboarding.

### Files Created
- **Root AGENTS.md** (166 lines): Complete project overview, tech stack, coordinate systems, anti-patterns
- **teleop_xr/AGENTS.md** (58 lines): Python backend (FastAPI, WebSocket, RUB↔FLU transforms)
- **teleop_xr/ik/AGENTS.md** (59 lines): JAX IK system (PyrokiSolver, relative motion control)
- **teleop_xr/ik/robots/AGENTS.md** (47 lines): Robot definitions (Franka, H1, TeaArm, OpenArm)
- **tests/AGENTS.md** (41 lines): Test suite patterns (pytest, anyio, mocking)
- **webxr/src/xr/AGENTS.md** (56 lines): Core WebXR (ECS systems, video streaming, console logs)
- **webxr/src/components/AGENTS.md** (49 lines): UI components (dashboard, Radix UI, Tailwind)

### Key Improvements
**Unique Patterns Documented:**
- Console log streaming: Quest headset → Python terminal via WebSocket
- RAM (Resource Asset Manager): On-demand URDF fetching from GitHub
- UIKitML: Custom VR panel markup (XML → JSON)
- VR-in-AR simulation: `immersive-ar` + opaque skybox

**Anti-Patterns Cataloged:**
- ECS: Never parent panel to handle entities (manual transform sync required)
- Orchestration: Always commit `.sisyphus/` files with code changes
- Python: Use PC timestamps for ROS TF (avoid headset drift)
- IK: Deadman Rule (both grips required for engagement)

**Architecture Mapped:**
- Hybrid monorepo: Python root + Next.js subfolder (no workspace orchestration)
- Coordinate systems: RUB (WebXR) ↔ FLU (ROS2) transforms
- Relative motion IK: `Target = Robot_Init + (XR_Current - XR_Init)`
- ECS pattern: Game engine approach vs React-Three-Fiber

**Complexity Hotspots Identified:**
- `teleop_xr/__init__.py`: 817L monolith (WebSocket handler, refactor candidate)
- `scripts/configure_sphere_collision.py`: 1107L GUI with deep nesting
- `teleop_xr/ros2/__main__.py`: 641L ROS2 bridge with message transforms

### Impact

### Motivation

- Enable `dhcp-snooping` and `arp-inspection` blocks in `templates/access_stack.j2` so access switches enable these protections for all enabled VLANs.

author: vercel[bot]
body:
# Vercel Web Analytics Implementation

## Summary
Successfully implemented Vercel Web Analytics on the coffee-fortune project, a plain HTML site with no framework dependencies.

## Changes Made

### Modified Files:
1. **index.html** - Added Vercel Web Analytics tracking scripts
2. **coffee_fortune.html** - Added Vercel Web Analytics tracking scripts

### Implementation Details:

For this plain HTML project, I followed the HTML implementation instructions from the Vercel Web Analytics documentation:

#### Analytics Scripts Added:
Both HTML files now include the following scripts in the `<head>` section, just before the closing `</head>` tag:

```html
<script>
    window.va = window.va || function () { (window.vaq = window.vaq || []).push(arguments); };
</script>
<script defer src="/_vercel/insights/script.js"></script>
```

### Technical Notes:

1. **No Package Installation Required**: Since this is a plain HTML site (no package.json), there's no need to install the `@vercel/analytics` npm package.

2. **No Route Support**: The HTML implementation doesn't include automatic route tracking, which is acceptable for a simple single-page application like this coffee fortune teller.

3. **Line Ending Conversion**: The original files had Windows-style (CRLF) line endings, which were converted to Unix-style (LF) line endings during the implementation for better cross-platform compatibility.

4. **Both Files Updated**: Since the project has two HTML files (`index.html` and `coffee_fortune.html`), both were updated to ensure consistent analytics tracking across the site.

### Next Steps for Deployment:

Once deployed to Vercel:
1. The analytics will automatically start tracking visitors and page views
2. Users can verify the setup by checking for a Fetch/XHR request to `/_vercel/insights/view` in the browser's Network tab
3. Analytics data will be available in the Vercel dashboard under the Analytics tab

### How It Works:

- The first script initializes the `window.va` function and sets up a queue for analytics events
- The second script (loaded with `defer`) fetches the actual tracking script from `/_vercel/insights/script.js`
- This route is automatically created by Vercel after enabling Web Analytics on the project

---

body:
Establishes structured task management for the GeoSpatial Data Quality Agent thesis project with 57 backlog items across 4 development phases.

## Core Deliverables

- **Product Backlog** (`PRODUCT_BACKLOG.md`): 57 tasks organized into 17 epics, ~500 story points
  - Phase 1: Core Functionality (20 items) - infrastructure, file ingestion, basic validation
  - Phase 2: Agent System (10 items) - LangGraph workflow, AI agents
  - Phase 3: UI/UX Polish (11 items) - dashboard, correction workflow
  - Phase 4: Evaluation & Documentation (9 items) - testing, thesis writing
  - Each item includes: priority (P0-P3), story points, acceptance criteria, dependencies

- **Process Documentation** (`BACKLOG_MANAGEMENT.md`): Prioritization framework (MoSCoW), estimation guidelines, sprint planning workflow

- **Sprint Templates**: Reusable template + example Sprint 1 with 7 infrastructure tasks

- **GitHub Issue Templates** (`.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/`): Standardized templates for features, bugs, user stories, documentation

- **Quick Start Guide** (`BACKLOG_QUICKSTART.md`): Onboarding and common workflows

## Structure

```
PRODUCT_BACKLOG.md           # Master backlog (all 57 tasks)
BACKLOG_MANAGEMENT.md        # Process guidelines
SPRINT_BACKLOG_TEMPLATE.md   # Reusable sprint template
sprints/sprint-01.md         # Example first sprint
.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/      # 4 issue templates
```

## Usage

**Sprint Planning:**
```bash
cp SPRINT_BACKLOG_TEMPLATE.md sprints/sprint-XX.md
# Select items from PRODUCT_BACKLOG.md based on priority and capacity
```

**Task Tracking:**
Each backlog item follows consistent format with priority, story points, status (⬜/🚧/✅), acceptance criteria, and dependencies.

**Estimation Scale:**
1-2 points (< 4hrs), 3-5 points (4-8hrs), 8-13 points (1-2 days), 21+ points (needs breakdown)

Updated README with backlog references. Added `.gitignore` for Python/Node artifacts.

body:
### Motivation
- The dashboard loaded scores by `job_id` only which can return scores across owners and leak/misattribute data when `job_id` or `candidate_id` is reused.  
- `job_insights` used the same `list_by_job(job_id=...)` call so counts and distributions could be computed from another owner’s scores, requiring owner-scoped enforcement.

### Description
- Add an optional `owner_id` field to `ScoreResult` and include it in the serialized payload via `ScoreResult.as_dict()` in `hirerank/scoring/models.py`.
- Propagate an optional `owner_id` into `compute_score` in `hirerank/scoring/engine.py` so generated scores may carry tenant context.
- Update `ScoringRepository` in `hirerank/storage/scoring_repository.py` so `save()` accepts an optional `owner_id` and stores records namespaced as `<owner_id>:<job_id>:<candidate_id>` when an owner is present, and change `list_by_job()` to require `owner_id` and filter by the owner-qualified prefix and payload owner.
- Change dashboard service calls in `hirerank/dashboard/service.py` to use `scoring_repo.list_by_job(owner_id=..., job_id=...)` for both `list_candidates_for_job` and `job_insights` so reads are owner-scoped; legacy un-namespaced score entries will not be returned by the new owner-scoped listing.

### Testing
- No automated tests were run for these changes.

OTP authentication failed intermittently when users typed their email with different casing between requests (e.g., "User@Example.com" → "user@example.com"). ## Changes **Database Adapter** (`packages/auth/src/lib/md-pg-drizzzle-adapter.ts`) - Import `normalizeEmail` from shared functions - Normalize email identifiers to lowercase during token creation and lookup ```typescript // Token creation - ensure consistent storage const normalizedData = { ...data, identifier: normalizeEmail(data.identifier), expires: data.expires.toISOString(), }; // Token lookup - case-insensitive matching const normalizedIdentifier = normalizeEmail(data.identifier); const [token] = await client .select() .from(verificationTokens) .where( and( eq(verificationTokens.identifier, normalizedIdentifier), eq(verificationTokens.token, data.token), ), ); ``` No changes to provider configuration or token hashing - the intermittent nature of failures indicated pure case-sensitivity issue, not configuration problems.

## Summary

Implement Phase 1, Step 1 of Issue #84 (Headless Mode Architecture) — define the foundational `DispatchBackend` interface that abstracts dispatch operations from GitHub.

## Changes

### New Module: `packages/core/src/backend.ts`

**Interface:**
- `DispatchBackend` — Core abstraction with methods for:
  - `listIssues()`, `listPRs()` — Situational awareness
  - `getIssue()`, `getPR()` — Detail fetching
  - `createIssue()`, `createPR()` — Artifact creation
  - `addComment()` — Issue/PR comments
  - `getRepoState()` — Git status
  - `applyChanges()`, `commit()`, `push()` — Code operations

**Types:**
- Issue types: `Issue`, `IssueComment`, `IssueState`, `IssuePriority`
- PR types: `PullRequest`, `PRFile`, `PRState`
- Options: `ListIssuesOptions`, `ListPRsOptions`, `CreateIssueInput`, `CreatePRInput`
- Results: `IssueResult`, `PRResult`, `ApplyResult`
- Config: `FileBackendConfig`, `GitHubBackendConfig`

**Utilities:**
- `extractPriority()` — Extract P0-P3 from labels
- `slugify()` — Generate URL-safe slugs
- `createBackend()` — Factory function (throws until implementations ready)

### Tests
- 24 new unit tests
- 398 total tests passing

## Architecture

```
                    ┌─────────────────────┐
                    │   DispatchBackend   │
                    │      (interface)    │
                    └──────────┬──────────┘
                               │
           ┌───────────────────┼───────────────────┐
           ▼                                       ▼
┌─────────────────────┐                 ┌─────────────────────┐
│    GitHubBackend    │                 │     FileBackend     │
│                     │                 │                     │
│  - gh issue list    │                 │  - input/issues/*   │
│  - gh pr create     │                 │  - output/patches/* │
│  - Real commits     │                 │  - Unified diffs    │
└─────────────────────┘                 └─────────────────────┘
```

## Next Steps (Phase 1)

- [ ] Step 2: Implement `GitHubBackend` — wrap existing `gh` CLI calls
- [ ] Step 3: Implement `FileBackend` — file-based input/output
- [ ] Step 4: Inject backend into `DispatchContext`

- Enables: SWE-bench evaluation, CI/CD integration, offline development

Bug: when a warm cache exists but the raw window has fewer tokens than `compact_max_tokens` (2000), the code was discarding the cached summary and only sending raw messages. This meant Claude only saw the last few messages instead of days of compacted context.

The 'skip if small' optimization makes sense for cold cache (small channel, nothing to compact), but was incorrectly applied to warm cache too.

**After:** includes the cached summary covering days of history

author: marcusquinn
body:
## Summary

- Add `backup_db()` / `restore_db()` helpers and `backup` / `restore` commands for supervisor DB safety and manual recovery
- Backup automatically before destructive schema migrations (t128.8 table rename/recreate, t148 table rename/recreate)
- Fix t128.8 migration: replace `INSERT INTO tasks SELECT * FROM tasks_old` with explicit column list to prevent column count mismatch when migrations run out of order

## Root Cause

The t128.8 migration used `SELECT *` to copy data from the old table to the new one. If a prior `ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN` migration had already added columns (e.g., `issue_url`, `diagnostic_of`, `triage_result`), the column count would mismatch and the migration would fail. Since the old table was already renamed at that point, a failed transaction could leave the DB in an inconsistent state with no recovery path.

Additionally, no backup was taken before any destructive migration, so there was no way to recover from a failed migration.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `supervisor-helper.sh` | Add `backup_db()` with SQLite `.backup`, timestamped copies, auto-prune to 5 |
| `supervisor-helper.sh` | Add `restore_db()` with validation and pre-restore safety backup |
| `supervisor-helper.sh` | Add `cmd_backup` / `cmd_restore` commands |
| `supervisor-helper.sh` | Backup before t128.8 and t148 destructive migrations |
| `supervisor-helper.sh` | Fix t128.8 `SELECT *` → explicit column list |
| `TODO.md` | Add t162 task entry |

- `bash -n` syntax check: pass
- `shellcheck -S error`: zero violations
- State machine tests: 69/69 pass (1 skip expected)
- Functional test: backup/restore cycle verified with test DB

body:
When running two doco-cd instances watching different subdirectories of the same repo, the auto-discover cleanup treats the other instance's stacks as obsolete and tries to destroy them every poll cycle.

**My setup:**
```
apps/
├── swarm/    # auto-deployed by doco-cd (SWARM=true, 30+ stacks)
├── compose/  # auto-deployed by doco-cd-compose (SWARM=false, 2 stacks)
└── infra/    # manual deploy, not auto-discovered
    ├── doco-cd/          # watches apps/swarm/
    └── doco-cd-compose/  # watches apps/compose/
```

**doco-cd (swarm):**
```yaml
DOCKER_SWARM_FEATURES: "true"
POLL_CONFIG: |
  - url: https://github.com/wajeht/home-ops.git
    reference: refs/heads/main
    interval: 60
    deployments:
      - working_dir: apps/swarm
        auto_discover: true
        auto_discover_opts:
          delete: true
```

**doco-cd-compose:**
```yaml
DOCKER_SWARM_FEATURES: "false"
POLL_CONFIG: |
  - url: https://github.com/wajeht/home-ops.git
    reference: refs/heads/main
    interval: 60
    deployments:
      - working_dir: apps/compose
        auto_discover: true
        auto_discover_opts:
          delete: true
```

Both instances share the same repo URL. The cleanup queries ALL containers with `cd.doco.deployment.auto_discover=true` and filters only by repo URL, so the compose instance marks every swarm stack as "obsolete" (and vice versa).

**Fix:** Also check `cd.doco.deployment.working_dir` during cleanup. Only consider stacks under the same base path as the current instance's deployments.

body:
## Summary

Adds typealias resolution to the type search tool. Previously, searching for `UIView` would not find a class like `class MyView: ViewAlias` where `typealias ViewAlias = UIView`. Now typealias chains are resolved in both directions:
- Searching by alias name (e.g. `Theme`) finds conforming types
- Searching by original type (e.g. `Stylable`) finds types conforming through aliases
- Chained aliases (e.g. `AppTheme → Theme → Stylable`) are fully resolved

## Key Changes

- **`SwiftParser`**: Handle `source.lang.swift.decl.typealias` AST kind — extract target type from source text via byte offsets and create `ObjectFromCode` entries that act as virtual inheritance links
- **`ObjectFromCode`**: Add `isTypealias` flag to distinguish alias entries from real types
- **`TypesSDK.countTypes`**: Filter out typealias entries from final results

## Additional Changes

- New test sample file `Tests/TypesSDKTests/Samples/Typealias.swift` with protocol alias, class alias, and chained alias scenarios
- 4 new tests covering all typealias search directions

## Checklist

- [x] Update `Sources/*/README.md` if public API changed — N/A, no public API changes

body:
### Motivation
- Ensure burn-fused ranged projectiles (arrows/slingshot) behave like a vanilla arrow that passed through a lit torch by becoming "lit" during flight so they can light torches, burn webs, and melt meltable ice the same way vanilla does.
- Apply this behavior at projectile spawn/commit time (not on impact) to match vanilla collision interactions with `Obj_Syokudai`, `BG_YDAN_SP`, and applicable ice actors.

### Description
- Added a helper `EnArrow_SetLitByFire` in `soh/src/overlays/actors/ovl_En_Arrow/z_en_arrow.c` that sets `actor.params = ARROW_NORMAL_LIT` and `collider.info.toucher.dmgFlags = DMG_ARROW_FIRE` to mirror vanilla lit-arrow state.
- Callout hook: invoked a new extern hook `FuseHooks_OnArrowProjectileSpawned` from `EnArrow_Shoot` immediately after `FuseHooks_OnArrowProjectileFired` so fuse logic runs at projectile spawn time.
- Implemented `FuseHooks_OnArrowProjectileSpawned` in `soh/soh/Enhancements/Fuse/Hooks/FuseHooks_Ranged.cpp` which checks the active ranged fuse slot, verifies the presence of a `Burn` modifier, and calls the new `EnArrow_SetLitByFire` for arrows/slingshot projectiles.
- Added a single minimal debug log when a projectile is converted: `Fuse::Log("[FuseDBG] BurnLitArrow: slot=%s proj=0x%04X mat=%d\n", ...)` to satisfy the logging requirement.

### Testing
- No automated runtime tests were executed because the game runtime/automated integration test environment was not available; changes were limited to the specified files and kept minimal and evidence-based.

## Summary

This PR introduces **Maritime Barge Drafting Operations** (codename: **Antigravity**, vector_gamma) as a new autonomous operational node within the SOL Lattice framework. The implementation replaces manual surveyors and drone flyovers with IoT sensor fusion and AI-driven draft survey analysis, targeting 0.998 accuracy for Gulf of Mexico inland barge operators.

## Key Changes

### Core Architecture
- **New Node Type**: `MaritimeBargeOps` added to lattice node hierarchy with safety-critical priority (k=3 consensus quorum required)
- **Agent Protocol**: Comprehensive `AGENT_PROTOCOL.md` defining the operational hierarchy (ARCHITECT → BUILDER/AUDITOR/SENTINEL) and inter-agent communication patterns
- **Blueprint Expansion**: Extended `freq_blueprint.py` with vector_gamma specifications including 9 sub-operations, regulatory standards (IMO Load Line, USCG 46 CFR, IMO A.749), and GCP service integrations

### Configuration & Deployment
- **SOL Config**: Added `maritime_barge_ops` node with ultrasonic IoT sensor type and 0.998 target accuracy
- **Vertex AI Playbook**: New Maritime Barge Drafting Operations playbook with SCAN > PROCESS > REPORT workflow
- **Custom Tools**: Three new Dialogflow tools:
  - Draft Survey Calculator (fore/mid/aft draft inputs, water properties)
  - Ballast Optimization Engine (trim and list control)
  - Maritime Compliance Checker (regulatory validation)

### Frontend & Visualization
- **Interactive Dashboard** (`public/index.html`): Full-featured simulation results UI with:
  - Real-time vessel metrics (60.96m LOA, 3,200 MT deadweight)
  - Draft survey calculations using Simpson's rule
  - Stability assessment (GM, GZ, freeboard, under-keel clearance)
  - Ballast tank distribution visualization (6 tanks)
  - Regulatory compliance matrix (4 standards, all PASS)
  - Cost analysis: **98.7% savings vs manual** ($159,887/yr), **99.8% vs drone** ($1M+/yr)

### Infrastructure
- **Firebase Hosting**: Added `.firebaserc` and `firebase.json` for deployment
- **Security Headers**: X-Frame-Options: DENY, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff

## Implementation Details

### Governance Integration
- Maritime operations require **k=3 consensus quorum** (same as Strategic OP)
- Full FREQ LAW compliance enforcement via GOVEngine VETO authority
- All operations logged to BigQuery audit trail with 9 event types

### Workflow Pipeline
1. **SCAN**: IoT sensor ingestion (6 ultrasonic draft sensors)
2. **PROCESS**: Draft calculation, displacement computation, ballast optimization, stability assessment
3. **GOVERNANCE**: FREQ LAW validation + k=3 consensus + VETO check
4. **REPORT**: Operational report, cost analysis, audit trail generation

### Regulatory Compliance
- IMO Load Line Convention (draft within marks)
- USCG 46 CFR Subchapter S (minimum freeboard)
- IMO Resolution A.749(18) (metacentric height)
- All checks automated and logged

### Cost Economics

- **Deployment timeline**: Phase 3 (simulation to hardware) with GCP Startup Program credits

- Stability metrics within acceptable range (GM: 11.573m, Risk: LOW)

gets filtered out.

- bin-openapi-manager: Add rtcp_stats object to SIP messages response schema

author: brian14708
body:
Extends Config initialization to automatically instantiate subclasses
declared via type annotations (e.g., sub: SubConfig), not just direct
assignments (e.g., sub = SubConfig).

Type Safety Benefits:
- 'sub = SubConfig' assigns the class itself, making type checkers infer
  type[SubConfig] (the class), breaking autocomplete and type checking
- 'sub: SubConfig' declares an instance annotation, allowing type checkers
  to correctly infer SubConfig (an instance) for proper IDE support
- This commit makes the type-safe pattern work at runtime

## Summary

- **31 integration tests** against Docker Compose with 5 PostgreSQL 16-alpine containers simulating MindMirror (4 DBs) and interlinear (1 DB) architectures
- **6 production bugs fixed** found by adversarial review of PRs 3 and 5 against the PR 6 test plan
- All **1344 tests pass** (1313 unit + 31 integration)

## What's tested

| Test file | Tests | Coverage |
|-----------|-------|----------|
| `test_mindmirror_source.py` | 8 | L2 vec sync: connect, discover, serialize, cross-domain query |
| `test_mindmirror_graph.py` | 11 | L3 graph: constraints, FK→edges, CHECK→rules, catalog detection, cross-DB edges |
| `test_interlinear.py` | 5 | Supabase patterns: JSONB, multilingual, CASCADE, M2M junctions |
| `test_unified_ingestor.py` | 5 | Ergonomic API: from_url, targets, batch_size |
| **conftest.py** | — | FakeEmbedding, FakeVectorIndex, asyncpg readiness probes |

## Bug fixes (from adversarial review)

1. **Junction table catalog detection** — `_items` suffix no longer marks `meal_food_items` as catalog (checks FK count)
2. **FK classification priority** — CASCADE now overrides `_template_id` pattern (habit_events → PART_OF, not INSTANCE_OF)
3. **`apply_cross_db_edges()` was a no-op** — now creates schema-level nodes and edges
4. **Cross-DB dedup order** — user identity edges (BELONGS_TO) discovered first, not overridden by naming convention (USES)
5. **`confdeltype` bytes vs str** — asyncpg returns `b'c'`, not `'c'`; cast to `::char` in SQL
6. **Invalid UUID fixtures** — non-hex prefixes (`l`, `v`, `m`, etc.) replaced with valid hex

```bash
docker compose -f tests/integration/docker-compose.yml up -d
sleep 10
pytest tests/integration/ -v -m integration
docker compose -f tests/integration/docker-compose.yml down -v
```

Closes #52

author: copilot
body:
The bit-plane decoder has a synchronization bug causing coefficient corruption in round-trip encode/decode operations. Manifests with 3+ non-zero coefficients; 1-2 coefficients work correctly. Affects 33 tests (2.4% of suite).

## Investigation Results

**Symptom**: Position 3 decoded as `-1` instead of `0` for input `[100, 0, 0, 0, 0, -50, 0, 0, 0, 0, 25, 0, ...]`

**Verified**:
- Encoder and decoder process identical operations (33 sig-prop, 15 mag-ref, 68 cleanup)
- Both make same RLC eligibility decisions
- Both use same arithmetic coding contexts (`sigPropLL_LH_0`)
- Bit-stream desynchronizes by final bit-plane:
  - Encoder writes: `Pos[3] isSig=false` 
  - Decoder reads: `Pos[3] isSig=true` (wrong bit position)

**Root Cause Hypothesis**: Inline state updates during cleanup pass (`states[idx].insert(.significant)`) create subtle timing differences in neighbor calculations that accumulate across bit-planes.

## Recommended Fix

Implement deferred state updates per `CLEANUP_PASS_FIX.md`:
1. Collect significance changes during cleanup pass iteration
2. Apply state updates after processing complete stripe
3. Ensures neighbor calculations use consistent state snapshot

Alternatively: Add bit-level MQ-coder instrumentation to identify exact divergence point.

## Test Impact

- 1,314 tests passing (97.6%)
- 33 tests failing (all bit-plane round-trip scenarios)
- No regressions introduced by investigation

author: rockoder
body:
### Selected Hacker News Posts
- [We mourn our craft](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=46926245)
- [France's homegrown open source online office suite](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=46923736)
- [Software factories and the agentic moment](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=46924426)

### Selection Justification
- **Craft/Specification:** High disagreement and anxiety in the community regarding the loss of "deep" coding skills. Cleared the bar by identifying that the "loss" is actually a migration of the source of truth to a higher layer of abstraction.
- **Digital Sovereignty:** Cleared the bar by identifying that the dominant narrative (feature parity) misses the strategic importance of the coordination environment.
- **Unit Cost of Code:** Cleared the bar by addressing the recurring confusion that more code generation equals more value, identifying the super-linear growth of validation debt.

### Conceptual Gaps Identified
- **Craft:** The industry is conflating the collapse of implementation costs with the disappearance of complexity; the complexity has merely moved to the specification layer.
- **Sovereignty:** Sovereignty is often misidentified as data locality, when it is actually about the agency to define organizational behavior via software metaphors.
- **Unit Cost:** The transition of code from an asset to a liability when its marginal cost of production hits zero.

### Essay Mapping
- **"The Specification Debt"** maps to *We mourn our craft*.
- **"The Sovereignty of the Environment"** maps to *France's office suite*.
- **"The Unit Cost of Code"** maps to *Software factories*.

### Commenter Quotations
- "I find it unsettling how many people in the comments say that they don't like writing code. Feels aliens to me." — *Ronsenshi*
- "Independence has a price. We as Europeans should be ready to pay it." — *okanat*
- "Software engineers are scared of designing things themselves." — *ipsento606*
- "If you haven't spent at least $1,000 on tokens today per human engineer, your software factory has room for improvement" — *Alex_L_Wood* (Highlighting the volume-centric incentive)

author: meteosimaji
body:
### Motivation
- Simplify browser URL safety policy to permit all `http`/`https` sites so browser downloads are not incorrectly blocked by a whitelist and IP/host checks.
- Ensure downloads triggered by the browser are validated using the actual download URL rather than only the navigation target to avoid false positives and failed downloads.

### Description
- Simplified `_is_safe_browser_url` to return `True` for `about:blank` and to accept any URL whose scheme is `http` or `https`, removing host/IP whitelist logic and the `BROWSER_TRUSTED_HOST_SUFFIXES` constant.
- Added `dl_url = getattr(download, "url", "") or ""` after `download = await download_info.value` and return an `unsafe_redirect` error if the download URL is not considered safe by `_is_safe_browser_url`.
- Changed the post-download navigation safety check to only apply `_is_safe_browser_url` when `urlparse(observed_url).scheme` is `http` or `https`, avoiding misclassification of non-http(s) schemes like `chrome-error://`.
- Improved `unsafe_redirect` error messages to include the actual URL for easier debugging and confirmed new variable names (`dl_url`, `observed_url`) do not collide with existing names.

### Testing
- Ran syntax checks with `python -m py_compile $(git ls-files '*.py')` which succeeded.
- Ran the full test suite with `pytest`, resulting in `61 passed` and `1 warning`.
- Performed repository searches with `rg -n "unsafe_redirect|_is_safe_browser_url|download"` to confirm the safety checks were updated consistently.

author: cappyzawa
body:
## Summary
- Add `create_manifest` job that creates multi-arch manifest lists combining amd64 and arm64 variants under the same tag
- Apply arch suffix to all architectures including amd64 for consistency

Currently, unqualified tags (e.g. `1.90.0-bookworm`) point to amd64-only images. On arm64 devices like Apple Silicon Macs, pulling these tags results in amd64 images running under emulation (Rosetta).

With this change, `docker pull ghcr.io/sksat/cargo-chef-docker:1.90.0-bookworm` will automatically select the correct architecture based on the host platform.

### Tag structure after this change
| Tag | Content |
|---|---|
| `:1.90.0-bookworm` | Multi-arch manifest (amd64 + arm64) |
| `:1.90.0-bookworm-amd64` | amd64 only |
| `:1.90.0-bookworm-arm64` | arm64 only |
| `:1.90.0-bookworm-i686` | i686 only |

### Backwards compatibility
The manifest list replaces the existing single-arch tag, but since the amd64 image is included in the manifest, existing amd64 users get the exact same image.

### Note on i686
i686 builds are marked as `continue-on-error` so that failures do not block multi-arch manifest creation, which only requires amd64 and arm64 images. i686 images are not included in the multi-arch manifest and remain available via their `-i686` suffixed tags as before.

### Verified on fork
Tested on `ghcr.io/cappyzawa/cargo-chef-docker` with Apple Silicon Mac:
- `ghcr.io/sksat/cargo-chef-docker:1.90.0-bullseye` → pulled **amd64** (current, no multi-arch)
- `ghcr.io/cappyzawa/cargo-chef-docker:1.90.0-bullseye` → pulled **arm64** (with multi-arch manifest)

author: robinnewhouse
body: ### Related Issue **Issue:** Part of Terminal-Bench hillclimb effort (follows #9154, #9156, #9159, #9161) ### Description Adds two concise, general-purpose prompt rules to improve agent output quality, tested and validated via Terminal-Bench benchmarks on Harbor. **Rule 1 — Output precision:** "When writing output files, produce exactly what the task specifies—no extra columns, fields, debug output, or commentary. Match the requested format precisely." **Rule 2 — Threshold iteration:** "When the task specifies numerical thresholds or accuracy targets, verify your result meets the criteria before completing. If close but not passing, iterate rather than declaring completion." These rules address two common failure patterns: - Agent adds extra columns/debug output to files (e.g., adding an `instance` column to a CSV that should only have `period,severity,count`) - Agent declares completion without verifying numerical results meet stated thresholds (e.g., Tm difference of 5.44°C when ≤5.0 was required) **What was excluded and why:** A third "no-cleanup" rule was tested and deliberately dropped. Despite using "STRICTLY FORBIDDEN" language, it failed to prevent the agent from deleting deployed content on `configure-git-webserver`, and caused a side-effect on `polyglot-c-py` (prevented legitimate build artifact cleanup). The cleanup behavior is too deeply trained to override via prompt rules. ### Test Procedure Tested on [Harbor](https://github.com/laude-institute/harbor) Terminal-Bench benchmark with Opus 4.6 (job `2026-02-07__16-15-00`, 6 targeted tasks on Modal): | Task | Baseline | With Rules | Rule | |------|----------|-----------|------| | log-summary-date-ranges | ❌ 0.0 | ✅ **1.0** | output precision | | dna-insert | ❌ 0.0 | ✅ **1.0** | threshold iteration | | mteb-leaderboard | ❌ 0.0 | ❌ 0.0 | (context overflow — not a prompt issue) | | polyglot-c-py | ❌ 0.0 | ❌ 0.0 | (build artifacts — tested no-cleanup, excluded) | | configure-git-webserver | ❌ 0.0 | ❌ 0.0 | (self-sabotage — no-cleanup rule failed) | | train-fasttext | ❌ 0.0 | ❌ 0.0 | (8% accuracy gap too large to iterate past) | **2 clear FAIL→PASS flips** from 4 insertions across 2 files. No regressions expected — both rules constrain behavior toward correctness. ### Type of Change - [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) ### Pre-flight Checklist - [x] Changes are limited to a single feature, bugfix or chore (split larger changes into separate PRs) - [ ] Tests are passing (`npm test`) and code is formatted and linted (`npm run format && npm run lint`) - [ ] I have created a changeset using `npm run changeset` (required for user-facing changes) - [ ] I have reviewed [contributor guidelines](https://github.com/cline/cline/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) ### Additional Notes These two rules follow [Cursor's agent best practices](https://cursor.com/blog/agent-best-practices): "Add rules only when you notice the agent making the same mistake repeatedly. Keep rules focused on essentials." Both are concise (1 line each), general-purpose, and empirically validated. ---- > [!IMPORTANT] > Adds rules for output precision and threshold iteration to improve agent output quality in multiple snapshot and template files. > > - **Behavior**: > - Adds rule for output precision: "Produce exactly what the task specifies—no extra columns, fields, debug output, or commentary. Match the requested format precisely." > - Adds rule for threshold iteration: "Verify numerical thresholds or accuracy targets before completing. If close but not passing, iterate rather than declaring completion." > - **Files**: > - Updates `rules.ts` and `template.ts` to include new rules in the rules template. > - Adds new rules to `anthropic_claude_sonnet_4-basic.snap`, `cline_devstral-basic.snap`, and `openai_gpt_3-basic.snap` among others. > > This description was created by [](https://www.ellipsis.dev?ref=cline%2Fcline&utm_source=github&utm_medium=referral) for e57b64654a976774f45557ede8ee6c5369c1998a.
